verdict.rationale: Apple's own specs publish 153GB/s memory bandwidth and the newsroom cites 32GB of memory capacity, which community posts corroborate as the M5 maximum. Apple also describes a unified memory architecture. However, no specific memory type (e.g., LPDDR generation, bus width or speed) appears in the vendor evidence. missing for 10: published memory type/generation, explicit first-party statement that 32GB is the capacity ceiling (stated only as 'with 32GB of memory capacity').

support.subject: As a developer, I can size memory-bound workloads from the vendor's own numbers — published memory type, capacity ceiling, and bandwidth (or spec detail complete enough to derive it)

citations.quote: The unified memory architecture enables the entire chip to access a large single pool of memory
32GB RAM limit on current M5 models.
